summary: No intent-graph update is required for the current /argo-init validator-bootstrap request. Implementation Design must instead adjust repository contracts and guardrails so /argo-init prepares the validator runtime assets under Argo-managed .github paths, applies the chosen package.json seeding policy, and leaves handoff JSON creation to later design work instead of bootstrap fabrication.

explicitTestcases.name: ARGO-INIT-VALIDATOR-BOOTSTRAP-CONTRACT
explicitTestcases.controlPoint: Invoke /argo-init in a target workspace that lacks some or all Argo validator bootstrap assets, including the validator script, the handoff schemas, and optionally package.json.
explicitTestcases.observationPoint: After bootstrap, the workspace contains .github/validator/script/validateStageHandoff.js and .github/argoschema/*.schema.json under Argo-managed paths; package.json is created when absent and otherwise only missing validate:handoff, validate:handoff:intent, and validate:handoff:implementation scripts are added, while pre-existing same-name scripts trigger conflict reporting instead of overwrite.
explicitTestcases.acceptanceBoundary: Implementation Design must materialize this as bootstrap contracts and critical verification guardrails for /argo-init without treating bootstrap as permission to fabricate missing design/KG handoff JSON files or to overwrite conflicting existing script names.
explicitTestcases.implementationNotes: This testcase directive is recorded in the handoff to satisfy the current handoff schema without rewriting design/KG/SystemArchitecture.json. It should be materialized as implementation-architecture guardrails rather than as a new read-only explicit testcase entry file.

openQuestions.question: How should Implementation Design classify workspaces that lack a usable Node/npm runtime after /argo-init has copied the validator assets and seeded package.json?
openQuestions.recommendedAnswer: Treat missing Node/npm runtime as an execution prerequisite failure that must be surfaced explicitly by the bootstrap flow or validation guardrail, rather than silently downgrading the validator contract.
openQuestions.reason: The chosen bootstrap policy now allows package.json creation, but validator execution still depends on an external runtime that bootstrap alone cannot guarantee. The next stage should preserve that boundary explicitly.

notes: This handoff intentionally keeps the current intent graph unchanged and pushes the requested behavior into Implementation Design contract updates plus bootstrap verification guardrails.
The selected policy permits /argo-init to create a minimal package.json when absent and to seed the three validate:handoff scripts only when they are missing.
If any of the target script names already exist, Implementation Design should preserve the no-overwrite rule and require explicit conflict reporting.
